title: Variables & string interpolation
prompt:
Write greet(string $name, int $age): string that returns exactly:

  Hello, NAME! You are AGE years old. Next year you'll be AGE+1.

Example: greet("Ana", 21) returns
  Hello, Ana! You are 21 years old. Next year you'll be 22.

Use variables and string interpolation (double quotes) rather than many concatenations.
starterCode:

function greet(string $name, int $age): string
{
    // TODO: compute next year's age, then interpolate both into the message
    return "";
}
hints: Double-quoted strings interpolate variables: "Hi $name" becomes Hi Ana. Single quotes do not.
Wrap variables in curly braces to be safe when text follows them directly: "{$age}" or "{$name}!".
Store $age + 1 in a variable first (e.g. $nextYear) and interpolate that; you can't do math inside the string.

tests.expected: Hello, Ana! You are 21 years old. Next year you'll be 22.
Hello, Bob! You are 30 years old. Next year you'll be 31.
Hello, JM! You are 0 years old. Next year you'll be 1.

solution:
<?php
function greet(string $name, int $age): string
{
    $nextYear = $age + 1;
    return "Hello, {$name}! You are {$age} years old. Next year you'll be {$nextYear}.";
}
